decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add … bookmarks with URL”; client round 1: “does what I need for saving…”
decisions.note: The presented URL-based save behavior conforms to the reference at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 defines editing as “with URL, title, description, and tags,” omitting the required note field; client round 1 gives general approval: “I’m happy with it as the first complete version.”
decisions.note: The closed edit-field presentation lacks note editing. The client neither identifies nor corrects that difference during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks” and “DELETE /api/bookmarks/:id”; client round 1 says the app meets the need for “removing bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion conforms to the reference at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: bookmarks support “tags”; client round 1 accepts the app for “organizing” bookmarks.
decisions.note: The presented ability to assign tags conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Live search across title, URL, description, and tags,” omitting note from the searchable fields; client round 1 only says it meets the need for “finding” bookmarks.
decisions.note: The search-field decision excludes the required note field. The client’s broad approval does not explicitly surface this difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “click any tag (in the sidebar or on a card) to filter” and “GET /api/bookmarks?q=&tag=” supports a tag filter; client round 1 approves the organizing/finding behavior.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag to filter its bookmarks conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “auto-fetch page titles/favicons from the URL” only as a “Possible next step,” establishing that automatic metadata collection is not in the delivered version; client round 1 calls the current version complete without mentioning the difference.
decisions.note: Automatic page metadata collection is deferred, and the offered future scope also does not cover all required metadata. Bare approval is not explicit acceptance of the divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” as a “Possible next step”; client round 1 responds only with general satisfaction with the current version.
decisions.note: Browser-HTML import is explicitly outside the delivered version. The client does not state the expectation or explicitly accept its absence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” as a “Possible next step”; client round 1 responds only with general satisfaction with the current version.
decisions.note: Browser-HTML export is explicitly outside the delivered version. The client’s bare approval does not qualify as accepted divergence.
